Meredith K. Lawson  
meredith.lawson@email.com | (555) 321-9876 | San Francisco, CA | linkedin.com/in/meredithklawson  

Data Scientist | Technical Lead | AI & Predictive Analytics Expert  

Experience  

Senior Data Scientist & Team Lead  
OptiMed Analytics, San Francisco, CA  
Feb 2018 - Present  
- I led a cross-functional team of 8 data scientists and engineers to develop a predictive analytics platform for hospital readmission rates, reducing patient readmissions by 15% and saving partner hospitals over $3.2M annually.  
- I architected and deployed machine learning models using Python (scikit-learn, TensorFlow) and Spark on AWS, improving model training time by 40% and enabling real-time decision support for 150K patients monthly.  
- I mentored 5 junior data scientists, establishing best practices in data preprocessing, model validation, and production deployment that decreased model errors by 22% across projects within the first year.  

Lead Data Scientist  
FinEdge Technologies, New York, NY  
July 2014 - Jan 2018  
- I built and led a team of 4 data scientists in developing fraud detection algorithms that reduced transaction fraud by 35%, protecting $120M in annual client revenue.  
- I decided to integrate GPU-accelerated deep learning models into the fraud pipeline using PyTorch, cutting false positives by 18% while maintaining a 98% detection rate.  
- I collaborated closely with product and engineering teams to ship analytics dashboards used by 500+ compliance officers, improving fraud response times by 50%.  

Data Scientist III  
Greenway Retail Solutions, Chicago, IL  
Aug 2012 - June 2014  
- I designed and implemented customer segmentation models using clustering and decision trees that increased targeted marketing campaign ROI by 40%, driving $5M incremental revenue in 18 months.  
- I led feature engineering initiatives on large retail datasets (10M+ transaction records) using SQL and R, reducing data processing times from hours to minutes and enabling faster insights.  
- I partnered with marketing and sales leadership to deploy A/B testing frameworks, guiding product strategy that improved customer retention rates by 12%.  

Data Scientist II  
TechNova Software, Austin, TX  
Jan 2010 - July 2012  
- I developed predictive maintenance models for industrial IoT sensors, decreasing machine downtime by 25% and saving $2M annually through early fault detection.  
- I implemented anomaly detection systems using time-series analysis and unsupervised learning techniques, contributing to a 30% reduction in unexpected equipment failures.  
- I collaborated on Agile teams to integrate analytics solutions into customer-facing applications with a user base of 50K+, improving client satisfaction ratings by 15%.

LINE EDIT 01 · SOURCE LINE

“- I decided to integrate GPU-accelerated deep learning models into the fraud pipeline using PyTorch, cutting false positives by 18% while maintaining a 98% detection rate.”

Integrated GPU-accelerated deep learning models using PyTorch into the fraud pipeline; false positives fell 18% while detection remained at 98%.

QUESTIONS WORTH ANSWERING

Prompts for your next revision.

These questions are not tied to a specific ranked fix. Use whichever ones surface a true, useful detail.

QUESTION 01

Why did you choose GPU-accelerated deep learning over the existing fraud approach, and what tradeoff did you accept?

Why it may help: The fraud bullet shows a technical decision and results, but not the constraint behind it.

QUESTION 02

How did the readmission platform handle decision support for 150K patients monthly?

Why it may help: The volume is substantial; the resume does not explain architecture, team process, or operational scale.

QUESTION 03

How did you maintain a 98% detection rate while cutting fraud false positives by 18%?

Why it may help: This result invites a concrete explanation of validation, monitoring, and risk controls.

QUESTION 04

What changed in your model validation practices before model errors fell 22%?

Why it may help: The mentoring bullet names the improvement but not the specific practice that produced it.

QUESTION 05

How did marketing and sales leadership use the A/B testing framework to change product strategy?

Why it may help: The partnership is clear, but the decision path from testing to strategy is not.
